messages:
Ashley (sales): Prospective client (regional bank) asked for a POC showing BYO-KMS/HSM integration. Main asks: perf impact, egress cost estimate, network/firewall diagram, and answers for their security questionnaire. They want something concise for procurement.
Ben (platform): Quick notes: BYO-KMS adds an auth + network hop for envelope unwraps. Ballpark latency penalty 10-40ms depending on KMS RTT and region. If they use cloud HSM with regional endpoint ~15ms; on-prem HSM could be higher.
Claire (crypto): Compliance questions first: do they need FIPS 140-2/3 attestation or dual-custody key ceremonies? If yes, timeline jumps (paperwork + attestation) and SOW needs to reflect onsite/remote key ceremony support.
Devon (solutions): For the POC we should show two modes: (A) Redwood-managed envelope keys (fastest path, no outbound unwraps) and (B) Customer-managed KEK with a lightweight sidecar that caches DEKs and performs unwraps locally to avoid per-request outbound calls.
Ashley (sales): They asked: "How do we price this? Will BYO add per-token costs?" They want numbers to justify procurement.
Ben (platform): Recommendation: present a small fixed connector/setup fee (one-time) + a variable ops estimate. For example: connector setup $X (depends on attestation/cross-account work), and per-100k unwrap ops estimate based on provider fees. Example calc: if their KMS charges $0.03 per 10k unwrappings, that's $0.30 per 100k; plus negligible egress bytes if inside same cloud region. We'll caveat with measured POC numbers.
Claire (crypto): Security guidance for caching: DEK cache TTL default 5 minutes, max entries limited by model/tenant (suggest 1000 keys), enforce LRU eviction, and require cache sealing at restart. Document rotation policy: rotate KEK per customer policy (monthly or quarterly), rotate DEKs more aggressively on suspicion. Include approved revocation playbook.
Devon (solutions): I'll prepare a tiny perf harness and a curl example they can run from their network so they measure true round-trips. Example command:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-BYO: true" \
  -d @payload.json
```
Run 1k requests with concurrency 8 and return p50/p95.
Ashley (sales): Also need an ops/network diagram listing required egress IPs/ports. They will raise this with infra team.
Ben (platform): Minimal: outbound HTTPS (443) to customer's KMS endpoints. If using on-prem appliances, we'll request IP allowlist and mTLS certs. If cloud HSM, use provider region endpoints (we'll list common ones: aws-kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, gcp-kms...). I'll draft sample iptables and a one-page diagram.
Claire (crypto): Question for customer: do they require audit event forwarding? We can optionally stream key usage logs to their SIEM (syslog/S3). Add that as an optional line item in the quote.
ops-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-2129 assigned to Devon (solutions)  POC planner due in 72h.
Ashley (sales): Action list: Devon -> perf harness + instructions; Ben -> ports/iplist + cost calc; Claire -> compliance checklist + rotation FAQ. I'll bundle into a POC email and attach a short slide with comparison table.
Ben (platform): I'll include an example cost table and show sensitivity bounds: best-case (same-region cloud HSM) vs worst-case (cross-region on-prem HSM with high RTT).
Claire (crypto): I'll add recommended config snippets for DEK cache and sample rotation commands.
Devon (solutions): If they want realtime help during perf tests, we can propose a 60-min on-call window to debug.
Ashley (sales): Thanks all. I'll schedule the kickoff once we have the artifacts. :thumbsup:
